sections.heading: Act fast
sections.content: Stroke can present suddenly. Warning signs include face drooping, arm weakness or numbness, speech trouble, sudden confusion, vision problems, dizziness, loss of balance, or a sudden severe headache.

sections.heading: Emergency response
sections.content: If stroke symptoms appear, call emergency services right away. Do not wait to see if symptoms improve, and do not drive yourself to care if emergency help is available.

sections.heading: Time matters
sections.content: Fast treatment can reduce disability and improve outcomes. Note the time symptoms started or when the person was last known well.
